cards.canonical_statement: For f(x,y)=x²+y², the first coordinate partial derivative at (a,b) is 2a.
cards.proof_strategy: Freeze the second coordinate and apply the one-variable square rule.
sketch_steps: setup: Fix the point (a,b).
restrict: Hold y=b and view f(x,b) as x²+b².
differentiate: Apply the square rule to x².
constant: The b² term has derivative zero.
conclude: The x-partial slope is 2a.

cards.canonical_statement: For f(x,y)=xy, the first coordinate partial derivative at (a,b) is b.
cards.proof_strategy: Freeze y=b and differentiate the linear function x ↦ xb.
sketch_steps: setup: Fix the point (a,b).
restrict: Hold y=b to obtain x ↦ xb.
linear: Use the derivative of the identity function.
scale: Multiply its slope by the constant b.
conclude: The x-partial slope is b.
